events.title: Battle of the Milvian Bridge
events.description: Roman Emperor Constantine the Great defeated his rival Maxentius at the Milvian Bridge near Rome. According to tradition, Constantine had seen a vision of a cross before the battle and ordered his soldiers to mark their shields with a Christian symbol.
events.significance: The victory made Constantine sole ruler of the Western Roman Empire and paved the way for the Christianization of the empire, profoundly shaping the course of European and world history.

events.title: Columbus Lands in Cuba
events.description: During his first voyage to the Americas, Christopher Columbus sighted the island of Cuba and landed on its northeastern coast, believing it might be part of mainland Asia. He named the island Juana.
events.significance: The landing marked an early step in European exploration and colonization of the Caribbean, leading to centuries of Spanish colonial rule in Cuba and major transformations for the indigenous peoples of the region.

events.title: Statue of Liberty Dedicated
events.description: President Grover Cleveland presided over the dedication of the Statue of Liberty on Bedloe's Island in New York Harbor. The statue, designed by Frédéric Auguste Bartholdi, was a gift from the people of France to the United States.
events.significance: The statue became one of the world's most recognizable symbols of freedom, democracy, and welcome to immigrants arriving in the United States.

events.title: Czechoslovak Independence Declared
events.description: The Czechoslovak National Committee in Prague proclaimed the independence of Czechoslovakia as the Austro-Hungarian Empire collapsed at the end of World War I. Tomáš Masaryk became the first president of the new republic.
events.significance: The founding of Czechoslovakia created a new democratic state in Central Europe and is still commemorated as a national holiday in the Czech Republic.

events.title: Cuban Missile Crisis Resolved
events.description: Soviet Premier Nikita Khrushchev announced that the Soviet Union would dismantle and remove its missiles from Cuba, ending the most dangerous confrontation of the Cold War after thirteen days of tension with the United States.
events.significance: The resolution averted a likely nuclear war between the superpowers and led to improved communication measures, including the Moscow-Washington hotline, and later arms control efforts.
